evidence: Unit tier: 61 tests, 61 pass, 0 fail on Node v22.23.2; JUnit XML written to tests/.results/unit.xml (gitignored). Covers the transition table and its no-ops, createRunState() starting values, jump edge semantics, delta clamp, score integer-ness and monotonicity, collision geometry, obstacle spawn/despawn, the trace record shape and endedAt pattern, the injected-clock wall-clock-jump scenario, and source hygiene.

Whole-run integration (tests/unit/run-loop.test.mjs) drives the real simulation modules with an injected clock and seeded random: a passive run ends on cactus contact; a jumping run survives more than twice as long and clears at least five cacti; the score sequence is non-decreasing and starts at 0; the trace record score equals the run-end score and sessionLengthMs is within 250 ms of the independently counted frame duration; three consecutive runs produce three records with no idle time leaking into any session length; 30 fps and 60 fps runs differ by under 35%.

Measured contrast, computed from src/render/palette.js over all 33 declared pairs, 0 failures. Text (AC-16, min 4.5:1): text on plate dawn 14.04, noon 11.91, dusk 15.80; heading on app shell dawn 13.64, noon 11.91, dusk 15.80. Non-text (AC-17, min 3:1): character vs sky 11.12 / 11.95 / 11.62; character vs ground line 3.30 / 3.49 / 3.55; cactus vs sky 10.34 / 10.90 / 11.00; cactus vs ground line 3.07 / 3.18 / 3.36; ground line vs sky 3.37 / 3.43 / 3.28; ground line vs ground 4.05 / 3.48 / 4.82; character accent vs character 7.19 / 9.89 / 8.91; cactus accent vs cactus 8.64 / 9.41 / 8.39; focus ring vs app shell 11.39 / 10.28 / 12.05.

Live DOM computed styles at http://localhost:4173/ (dawn variation): score readout, idle instruction, run-end title, final score, restart instruction and key legend all render #241033 on #FFE3A8 = 14.04:1, every background-color alpha exactly 1 (no partial transparency behind any text); page heading #FFE3A8 on #2B0F3A = 13.64:1.
Rendered-pixel sampling of the live canvas matched the declared palette exactly: sky #FFE3A8, ground #2B0F3A, ground line #B36A15, character #0E2A5E - what is drawn is what palette.js declares.

Browser observed (Chromium via the Browser pane, http://localhost:4173/): zero console errors and zero console output from the game on load; 16 resources, all same-origin static assets, zero cross-origin, nothing requested after load; performance.getEntriesByType('navigation').length === 1; localStorage, sessionStorage and document.cookie all empty; window.dinoDash frozen and non-writable, version 1, getState() 'idle', getScoreTrace() [], getBackgroundVariations() ['dawn','noon','dusk']; data-game-state='idle' on #dino-dash at bootstrap.
Input path observed in the browser: a Space keydown moved the state idle to running with defaultPrevented true and data-game-state updated to 'running'; the same handler covers Up Arrow.

AC-26 key sweep in the idle state: 46 distinct keys (Enter, Escape, Tab, all four arrows, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, PageUp/Down, F1/F5/F12, letters, digits, punctuation, modifiers, Meta) dispatched - no state change, no transition event, no key other than Space/Up Arrow prevented a default; the document contains zero table/dialog/menu/form/input/select elements and the rendered text contains none of leaderboard, settings, profile, lobby, catalogue, sign in, account.

Focus: exactly one focus stop exists (#dd-stage, tabindex=0, aria-labelled); the canvas has tabIndex -1 and aria-hidden=true; the stylesheet carries .dd-stage:focus and :focus-visible rules resolving --dd-focus to #9BE84A at 5 px with 4 px offset; the page contains zero form controls.

Visual verification: the real renderer and the real simulation were driven inside the page for a full 34-second, 339-point run and the frames captured. The idle, running (dawn), noon, dusk and collision scenes all render correctly - a navy/maroon dino with a contrasting accent belly and eye, green cacti with lime stripes, a coloured ground band with moving dashes, a coloured ground line and a sun, on cream / sky-blue / pale-pink skies. The collision frame shows the character in contact with a cactus at the moment the run ended. The result is colour-bearing, not the monochrome reference styling.

Playability: an autoplay driven only by obstacle positions cleared 35 cacti across 34 seconds and reached score 339, walking the background enumeration dawn to noon to dusk in order at scores 0/100/200 before colliding.

Boundary: the commit contains 29 files, all under src/, tests/ or docs/; zero paths outside. The product workspace D:/os-test/dino-dash has exactly the same git status as at session start. engineering/**, .development-os/**, DEVELOPMENT.md and development-os.config.json are untouched.
knownRisks: In-browser dynamic gameplay could NOT be observed end to end. The Browser pane never composited frames in this environment, so the tab stayed document.hidden and requestAnimationFrame fired zero times per second. Consequently the following were verified only through the Node integration tier driving the real simulation modules, not through a live browser run: the jump arc on screen, score accrual over time, the collision to run-end transition in the page, the run-end panel showing the final score, restart clearing obstacles without a reload, and window.dinoDash.getScoreTrace() containing records after real runs. The trace accessor was observed returning [] on a fresh page only.

No screenshots of the assembled page (canvas plus DOM text layer) exist. Screenshot capture failed with 'the Browser pane is not displayed'. The captured images are the canvas play field rendered by the real renderer, not the composited page. Playwright was installed to work around this but its Chromium binary never downloaded (the browser CDN appears blocked in this environment; the install exited 0 with an empty ms-playwright directory).

AC-05 was evidenced as 'the handler calls preventDefault on Space and Up Arrow' (defaultPrevented true, and no key beyond those two prevents anything). The trusted-event consequence - that the document scroll position does not move in a short viewport - was NOT observed, because trusted key delivery was unavailable.

AC-14's visible focus ring was verified as a parsed CSS rule with the correct resolved colour, not as a rendered outline: the browser window never held focus (document.hasFocus() false), so :focus did not match at measurement time.

AC-16/AC-17 rendered-pixel confirmation covers the dawn variation live; noon and dusk rendered pixels were sampled from the real renderer driven inside the page rather than from a live run. The static computation covers all three variations exhaustively.

src/package.json containing type module is a judgement call. Without it Node resolves src/**/*.js as CommonJS and no unit test can import the delivery. It is inside the WS-03 boundary and ignored by browsers, but WS-12 may prefer type module in the root package.json, which would make this file redundant.

src/game/simulation.js is an addition to the module list in ADR-002 section 4. It is on the DOM-free side of the boundary, so the boundary rule is unchanged, but the file list in the ADR no longer matches the tree exactly.

input/keyboard.js falls back from KeyboardEvent.code to KeyboardEvent.key. This was added because the automation harness in this environment dispatches key events with an empty code. It recognises the same two keys and adds no third one, but it is a deviation from a strict code-only reading of ADR-001's API floor.

tests/tools/static-server.mjs duplicates a responsibility ADR-005 section 2 assigns to WS-12. It exists because nothing runnable exists at this revision; it should be superseded, and the npm script form of the AC-30 commands still depends on WS-12.

AC-30 is not closed by this workstream: no package.json, no lockfile and no Playwright browser tier exist at this revision, so no clean-checkout npm ci and npm test run was performed, and no accessibility-evidence command exists beyond the unit tier's static contrast computation. Evidence has not been recorded under .development-os/evidence/ because that path is outside the WS-03 write boundary.

AC-18's judgement half (modern and colourful) is the product owner's under final_user_visible_acceptance and is not claimed here; only the objective half (three distinct hues per variation with HSV saturation above 0.25, and non-greyscale rendering) is evidenced.
ADR-003's open interpretation risk on AC-19 is unchanged: endedAt uses the Z designator for explicit UTC offset. A verifier requiring a numeric plus-minus HH:MM would read it differently.
The canvas is aria-hidden, so gameplay is not conveyed to assistive technology. This is ADR-002's recorded known limitation, carried forward, not a satisfied requirement.
Gecko was neither tested nor claimed, per DEC-20260809-001 and ADR-001. No engine-specific API is used anywhere in the delivery.
